headline: Approved shed application at 240 Cards Pond Road and recommended two subdivision applications move forward
summary: The committee approved prior meeting minutes, then reviewed three applications. It approved a shed construction request at 240 Cards Pond Road. It recommended Administrative Officer Approval for the Egan Minor Subdivision at 11 Oak Dell Street with four conditions. It recommended the TNT Real Estate Plat subdivision at 871 & 889 Broad Rock Road be forwarded to the Planning Board with four conditions.
decisions: Approved the April 8, 2026 and June 10, 2026 TRC meeting minutes by majority vote, with Mr. Jordan abstaining.
Approved the Mallin application to construct two sheds at 240 Cards Pond Road, with the condition that a building permit be applied for prior to any work.
Recommended Administrative Officer Approval for the Egan Minor Subdivision at 11 Oak Dell Street, AP 48-3, Lot 106, with four items to be addressed.
Recommended the TNT Real Estate Plat application at 871 & 889 Broad Rock Road, AP 33, Lots 11 & 12 be forwarded to the Planning Board with four items to be addressed.

plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Technical Review Committee (TRC)   
REVISED  Meeting Minutes 
Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 11:00 AM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
 
 
A. Call to Order & Roll Call 
Mr. Rabbitt called the meeting to order at 11:00 a.m. 
 
ROLL CALL: 
Dennis Bernier, UFD; Mark Conboy, Town Engineer; Rich Bourbonnais, Director of Public Services; Jamie Gorman, 
Building Official; and Paul Jordan, Planning Board.  Also present were James Rabbitt, Director of Planning; Brian Wagner, 
Deputy Director of Planning; and Curtis Dufour, Principal Planner.  
B. Approval of Minutes: 
The following motion, made by Mr. Gorman, was duly seconded by Mr. Bourbonnais; Mr. Jordan abstained; passed by a 
majority vote. 
Motion: "The Technical Review Committee hereby approves the listed meeting minutes, as presented." 
 1. April 8, 2026, TRC Meeting 
 2. May - No meeting. 
 3. June 10, 2026, TRC Meeting 
 4. July - No meeting. 
C. TRC Review: 
 1. Mallin - Coastal Community Overlay District (CCOD) Review.  Request to construct two (2) 3' x 4' x 7' sheds 
using wood construction.  The structures are proposed to be attached to the east side of the existing house 
(total of 2,459 square feet) located at 240 Cards Pond Road, 16E15, AP 92-1, Lots 9-183.  Timothy Mallin, 
applicant; Joan Mallin & Kathleen Crawley, Et als, owners. 
Timothy Mallin, applicant, appeared to present the application.  
Mr. Gorman reviewed the criteria required for the request, and stated that after TRC approval, the applicant should 
apply for a building permit. 
Mr. Rabbitt stated that he, along with the other members of the TRC, has no issue with this application. 
 
The following motion made by Mr. Gorman, was duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, passed unanimously. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Technical Review Committee hereby approves the application, with the clarification that 
a Building Permit does need to be applied for, prior to the start of any work." 
 2. Egan Minor Subdivision — Preliminary Plan Review.  Property located at 11 Oak Dell Street, AP 48-3, Lot 
106.  Christopher and Patricia Egan, applicant/owner. 
Christopher Egan appeared to present the application. 
Discussion ensued regarding: two existing driveways; no new curb cuts required; the ability to come back at a later time 
to widen a driveway, but will require a permit from DPS; a new sewer line to Oakdell Street must be completely 
separate, can not have sewer lines running through other properties or tie them in; when a building permit is applied 
for, applicant will be asked to do a soil erosion control permit.
Mr. Rabbitt expressed concern about the intended utilization of an existing driveway on the east side of Oakdell, which 
will be on a property line; this may cause a problem with driveway maintenance. Mr. Rabbitt suggested that the 
driveway be slid away from the property line or a Maintenance and Use Easement be granted over existing property. 
 Mr. Rabbitt also stated that site lines for both driveways need to be cleared of all vegetation and need to be evaluated 
during the Building Permit application process.  
 
Mr. Rabbitt listed the four recommendations to any approval language: 
1. Site lines need to be clear for all the driveways reviewed and be approved by the Department of Public Service (DPS). 
2. The driveway for the new unit will need to be moved to the west, away from the property line, reviewed and 
approved by DPS prior to the issuance of a building permit. 
3. Separate sewer, devoid of any easements, will need to be shown and provided on each lot. 
4. During the building permit process, a soil erosion and soil control plan, which will also include a storm water 
management plant, will need to be submitted. 
 
Mr. Egan questioned whom he needed to engage for the Soil Erosion plan — Mr. Bourbonnais informed him that it 
generally requires an engineer to show the calculations that you are meeting the runoff requirements.  Increases in 
runoff, up to a 10-year storm; if an underground infiltration or an above-grade rain garden, those things need to be sized 
properly, to show erosion control.  Not something the contractor normally does, but is information the contractor 
needs. 
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Jordan, duly seconded by Mr. Gorman, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion:  "The South Kingstown Technical Review Committee hereby recommends Administrative Officer Approval, with 
the above four items to be addressed by the applicant." 
 3. TNT Real Estate Plat - Administrative Subdivision w/Unified Development Review, located at 871 & 889 
Broad Rock Road, AP 33, Lots 11 & 12.TNT Real Estate Holdings, LLC., applicant; TNT Real Estate 
Holdings, LLC and Kaitlyn Fratus & Daniel Cross, owners of Lots 11 and 12, respectfully. 
Matthew Brown, of TNT Real Estate, LLC, applicant/owner, appeared to present the application.  Mr. Brown briefly 
explained the purpose of the application.  A brief discussion between the staff members regarding the reason the 
application requires TRC review and Planning Board Approval (two non-conforming lots). 
 
Mr. Rabbitt stated that many things are dealt with by the Planning Board, and/or conditioned upon the issuance of a 
building permit for any of the properties in regard to driveways, site lines, separate sewer, erosion, sediment control 
and storm water management plans.  To be clear, this is a proposal to move property lines, and this committee is not 
evaluating the effect it has on the development of the lot.   
 
The following motion, made by Mr. Bourbonnais, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, passed by unanimous vote. 
Motion: "The South Kingstown Technical Review Committee hereby recommends this application be forwarded to the 
Planning Board, with the above four underlined items to be addressed by the applicant."  
D. TRC Advisory Review: 
None 
E. Adjournment: 
The meeting adjourned at 11:25 a.m., by unanimous consent.
